\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{موج} (mauj)}{موج (mauj)}]{\ur{موج} (mauj) — a wave; a billow}

\label{lesson:UR-C434-mauj}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a straw, then the Urdu for to be uprooted.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{موج}}
\textbf{\ur{موج}} — \emph{mauj} — \textquotedblleft{}a wave; a billow\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سمندر} \ur{میں} \ur{اونچی} \ur{موجیں} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{samandar meṅ ū̃chī maujeṅ haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There are high waves on the sea.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{موج}} (\emph{mauj}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{mawj}, \textquotedblleft{}waves, surging\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mauj}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mauj}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{samandar meṅ ū̃chī maujeṅ haiṅ.} — There are high waves on the sea.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a straw, then the Urdu for to be uprooted, then say \emph{mauj} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{موج} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A wave; a billow\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دلدل} (daldal)}{دلدل (daldal)}]{\ur{دلدل} (daldal) — a marsh; a swamp}

\label{lesson:UR-C434-daldal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to be uprooted, then the Urdu for a billow.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دلدل}}
\textbf{\ur{دلدل}} — \emph{daldal} — \textquotedblleft{}a marsh; a swamp\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دریا} \ur{کے} \ur{پاس} \ur{ایک} \ur{دلدل} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{daryā ke pās ek daldal hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There is a marsh near the river.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دلدل}} (\emph{daldal}) is inherited: CDIAL lists Hindi \emph{daldal}, \textquotedblleft{}a marsh\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{dal}, \textquotedblleft{}quiver\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 6212): a marsh is ground that shakes underfoot.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{گھاٹ} (ghāṭ)}{گھاٹ (ghāṭ)}]{\ur{گھاٹ} (ghāṭ) — a landing place (on a river)}

\label{lesson:UR-C434-ghat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a billow, then the Urdu for a marsh.

\textbf{\ur{گھاٹ}} — \emph{ghāṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a landing place (on a river)\textquotedblright{}.

Masculine.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اچھالنا} (uchhālnā)}{اچھالنا (uchhālnā)}]{\ur{اچھالنا} (uchhālnā) — to toss (up); to throw up}

\label{lesson:UR-C434-uchhaalna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a marsh, then the Urdu for a landing place (on a river).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اچھالنا}}
\textbf{\ur{اچھالنا}} — \emph{uchhālnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to toss (up); to throw up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{موجوں} \ur{نے} \ur{کشتی} \ur{کو} \ur{اچھالا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maujoṅ ne kashtī ko uchhālā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The waves tossed the boat about.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{گیند} \ur{اچھالی}, \emph{us ne gend uchhālī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اچھالنا}} (\emph{uchhālnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{uchālnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to throw up\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{ut-śālayati}, \textquotedblleft{}causes to leap up\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 1848); \textbf{\ur{اچھلنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to bounce\textquotedblright{}, is its partner.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uchhālnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{uchhālnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maujoṅ ne kashtī ko uchhālā.} — The waves tossed the boat about.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a marsh, then the Urdu for a landing place (on a river), then say \emph{uchhālnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ڈبونا} (ḍubonā)}{ڈبونا (ḍubonā)}]{\ur{ڈبونا} (ḍubonā) — to dip; to sink (something)}

\label{lesson:UR-C434-dubona}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a landing place (on a river), then the Urdu for to toss (up).
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ڈبونا}}
\textbf{\ur{ڈبونا}} — \emph{ḍubonā} — \textquotedblleft{}to dip; to sink (something)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سارا} \ur{نے} \ur{دریا} \ur{میں} \ur{ہاتھ} \ur{ڈبوئے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sārā ne daryā meṅ hāth ḍuboe.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Sara dipped her hands in the river.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کشتی} \ur{ڈبوئی}, \emph{us ne kashtī ḍuboī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ڈبونا}} (\emph{ḍubonā}) is built on \emph{ḍūbnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to sink\textquotedblright{}, which comes from \emph{ḍubb}, a form CDIAL reconstructs (CDIAL 5561): this is the form for putting something under water.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍubonā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍubonā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sārā ne daryā meṅ hāth ḍuboe.} — Sara dipped her hands in the river.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a landing place (on a river), then the Urdu for to toss (up), then say \emph{ḍubonā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ڈبونا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To dip; to sink (something)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
